newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt seeks ways to enhance power competition.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt seeks ways to enhance power competition.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Thursday said the government wanted greater competition in electricity generation.
"We will be investigating options to introduce further competition in electricity generation," he said.
Peters on Thursday presented the government's 1997/98 budget.
Asked if the government planned to split the Electricity Corporation of New Zealand further, Peters said: "That is a very insightful observation."
"We believe there are far greater savings to be made for New Zealand consumers and business and we are signalling our intention to go down that track," he told a media briefing.
In 1995 the government split off Contact Energy from state-owned ECNZ. Both remain state owned, and the coalition government has said it is committed to retaining that ownership.
However, it has signalled it will sell eight small hydro stations to local operators.
The government has faced criticism that despite the Contact-ECNZ split and deregulation, the electricity industry has not achieved the level of competition desired by the government.
